solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dandy returned cereal in antique cupboard

parts.note: a beau is a fop or dandy

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the grain's name is read from its end

parts.note: teff is an Ethiopian cereal grass

explanation.surface: A fop has put his breakfast cereal back in an old cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Teff is little known outside Ethiopia; Azed often uses Chambers-only old spellings like this one for buffet.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauffet is an obsolete form of buffet, a sideboard or cupboard for displaying china.

clue.text: Punch ruined carousal

definitions.meaning: third meaning: a drinking spree or binge

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one short word: a punch, broke, and a boozy spree.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as a noun for a blow, an adjective for bankrupt, and a noun for a drinking bout.

clue.text: To propound theories about myth, he and I use mere waffle

indicators.note: waffle is muddled rambling talk, so the preceding words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people ramble pointlessly while offering theories about mythology.
explanation.definitionFit: Euhemerism explains myths as distorted history of real people, so to euhemerise is to theorise about myth that way.

clue.text: Fungus — farming in short must contain one

indicators.note: to contain something is to hold it inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: AGRIC is the short form of agriculture
A as the indefinite article means one

explanation.surface: Mushrooms must form part of any brief account of agriculture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Farming' looks like part of the surface story, but its abbreviation supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An agaric is a gilled mushroom, a common type of fungus.

clue.text: Old Scottish tenor did this with last bit of folk

parts.note: fec. abbreviates Latin fecit, 'made this', written beside an artist's signature

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter alone

parts.note: final letter of folk

explanation.surface: An old Scots singer performed this with the closing part of a folk song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenor' is not a singer but the purport or gist of something; FEC stands for fecit, the word artists put after their names.
explanation.definitionFit: In old Scots, feck means effect or purport, the same as tenor in the sense of general drift.

clue.text: Literary society paid money to hold ancient books, German

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so the payment surrounds what follows

parts.note: a fee is money paid
libri is Latin, the ancient tongue, for books
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A literary club paid out to keep old German volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient' points to Latin, the language of the ancient Romans.
explanation.definitionFit: The Félibrige is a Provençal literary association founded in 1854 to revive the language of southern France.

clue.text: Opposite of us up north, with the intention to be rid of English

indicators.note: being rid of something means it is thrown out, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: an aim is an intention
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Northerners say the opposite of us, intending to be free of the English.
explanation.walkthrough: THE AIM loses an E to give THAIM; 'up north' marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Thaim is the Scots form of them, the pronoun contrasted with us.

clue.text: Scottish bear top BBC official released from net

indicators.note: something released from a thing is let out of it, so those letters leave

parts.note: a dredge is a dragnet
the Director-General heads the BBC

explanation.surface: A Scottish bear has caught the head of the BBC in a net, then let him go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' is a verb, to endure. DREDGE without DG leaves DREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dree is a Scots verb meaning to endure or suffer, as in 'dree one's weird'.

clue.text: Draughtsman lumping it when extreme characters are switched

indicators.note: the two end letters trade places, each taking the other's position

parts.note: to lump it is to put up with something, being resigned to it

explanation.surface: A draughtsman puts up with it when his lettering gets swapped round.
explanation.walkthrough: RESIGNED with its first and last letters swapped becomes DESIGNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A draughtsman draws plans and designs, so a designer is a fair synonym.

clue.text: In gathering of spring grain, crop first half of cabbage

indicators.note: cropping trims off part, here the whole front half of the word

parts.note: kohlrabi is a cabbage with a swollen edible stem

explanation.surface: While harvesting spring grain, cut half of the cabbage too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' stands for India: rabi is India's spring harvest. Remove KOHL from KOHLRABI.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabi is the Indian grain crop sown in autumn and harvested in spring.

clue.text: Popular controller managing the ranch

indicators.note: managing suggests handling and arranging, so the letters are reorganised

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A well-liked boss is running the ranch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular' here means of the people, not well liked.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethnarch is a ruler of a people or province, so a governor over a nation.

clue.text: It's hard in varied tree range

definitions.text: It's hard in varied tree range

indicators.note: varied means changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
taken as written

explanation.surface: Among a range of mixed trees, this one is especially hard.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes in with the letters of TREE RANGE and the lot is mixed; the whole clue also describes the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenheart is a South American tree whose timber is famously hard and dense.

clue.text: Thicket has stunted old hedge

indicators.note: stunted means cut short in growth, so the word is shortened

parts.note: has cut to its contracted form 's
haw is an archaic word for a hedge or enclosure

explanation.surface: A dense wood contains an old, stunted hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' shrinks to its contraction 's, as in 'he's gone'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw is an old and dialect word for a small wood or thicket.

clue.text: Fortress devastation mostly overturned, dammit

indicators.note: overturned in a down light means flipped, so the shortened word reads backwards
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: the sack of a city is its devastation
bah is an exclamation of annoyance

explanation.surface: The fortress has been wrecked and toppled, and someone curses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dammit' is a separate exclamation, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A casbah is the citadel of a North African city, so a fortress.

clue.text: It has its own key, being within all eight? (10, two words)

indicators.note: within means inside, so the first word sits inside the following pair

parts.note: taken as written
ens is the philosophers' Latin for being or existence
a rowing eight is a crew

explanation.surface: Something with its own key, belonging inside all eight items.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'key' is the hexagonal Allen key made to turn it, not a lock key or a musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: An Allen screw has a hexagonal socket in its head, turned with a matching L-shaped tool.

clue.text: Fish to eat? He fumbled with it imbibing spirituous liquor

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the spirit goes inside
fumbled means handled clumsily, so those letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
raki is an aniseed spirit from Turkey and the Balkans

explanation.surface: A man fumbles his fish supper while knocking back spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The fish comes from New Zealand, where it is a popular table fish, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The terakihi is a New Zealand sea fish valued as food, hence one to eat.

clue.text: I'll provide stuff for those bowing — and scraping?

definitions.text: I'll provide stuff for those bowing — and scraping?

parts.note: surface reading: obsequious flatterers who bow and scrape

parts.words: I'll provide stuff for those bowing — and scraping
parts.note: setter's reading: a source of hair for violinists' bows, and a plant used for scouring

explanation.surface: Something offers material to fawning sycophants.
explanation.walkthrough: Violin bows are strung with hair from a horse's tail; the horsetail plant, rich in silica, was also used to scour pots.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the hair on a horse and the rush-like plant of that name fit, one for bowing and one for scraping.

clue.text: Fashion, integral part of futurism, I think

indicators.note: an integral part is built into the whole, so the letters lie inside the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the end of futurism and on into I think

explanation.surface: Fashion is, I believe, a key element of the futurist movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' is a verb here, to make or forge.
explanation.definitionFit: To smith is to forge or shape metal, so to fashion by hand.

clue.text: Fighting cock, beak ripping into old quail

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the jumbled letters enter the next word

parts.note: shag is an obsolete verb meaning to shake, as one who quails trembles

indicators.note: ripping tears things up, so those letters are torn apart and reset

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fighting cock's beak tears into an old quail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quail' is not the bird but the verb, to tremble.
explanation.definitionFit: A shakebag is a large fighting cock, a term from the old cockpit.

clue.text: Thyroid inhibitor hit a roué being treated

indicators.note: something being treated is processed and altered, so the letters change order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A womaniser is struck while under medical treatment for his thyroid.
explanation.definitionFit: Thiourea is a sulphur compound that suppresses thyroid hormone production, used as an antithyroid drug.

clue.text: A plate of insects from Roman province, second held back till last

indicators.note: a letter held back till last is moved from its place to the very end

parts.note: Gaul was a province of the Roman Empire

explanation.surface: A dish of insects from a Roman province, with the second course delayed till the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plate' is anatomy, not crockery. GAUL with its second letter moved to the end gives GULA.
explanation.definitionFit: The gula is a plate on the underside of an insect's head, forming part of its throat.

clue.text: Fishing vessel — or what she resembles closely?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a boat used for catching herring
second meaning, split in two: ..., a ringer being an exact lookalike

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading divides the answer as HER + RINGER: a dead ringer is someone's double.
explanation.definitionFit: A herringer is a boat for herring fishing, and the split form names her double.

clue.text: Arab with power vested in observance — one on the make

parts.note: Ar is a standard abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

indicators.note: something vested in another is placed within it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a rite is a religious observance
vis is Latin for force or power

explanation.surface: An Arab endowed with authority through ceremony is an opportunist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power' is Latin here, and 'vested in' tells you it sits inside the observance.
explanation.definitionFit: An arriviste is an ambitious social climber, someone out for advancement.

clue.text: Revered figure I cloaked in loose old gown

indicators.note: being cloaked in something means being wrapped inside it

parts.note: manto is an obsolete word for a loose cloak or gown, like a mantua
taken as written

explanation.surface: A venerated figure wraps himself in an old flowing robe.
explanation.walkthrough: The gown is an obsolete Chambers word, related to mantle and mantua.
explanation.definitionFit: A manito, or manitou, is a spirit or deity revered by Algonquian peoples.

clue.text: Backward lout retaining name as astringent

indicators.note: backward means facing the wrong way, so the word is read from its end
retaining means keeping hold of, so the reversed word wraps round the letter

parts.note: oik is British slang for an uncouth person
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A dim lout keeps his name as a harsh substance.
explanation.walkthrough: OIK turned round is KIO, which then takes N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Kino is a gum from tropical trees used as an astringent in medicine and tanning.

clue.text: Serving girls having to get right inside nasty spots

indicators.note: getting inside means entering, so one letter is put within the other word

parts.note: wens are cysts or unsightly lumps on the skin
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Serving women must have the right to get rid of their spots.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside WENS. Wrens were members of the Women's Royal Naval Service, Britain's women sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wrens were women serving in the Royal Navy, so serving girls in a military sense.

clue.text: Coarse linen that goes into the making of Lycra shirts

indicators.text: that goes into the making of
indicators.note: what goes into making something is a component inside it, so the letters sit within

parts.note: the letters span the end of Lycra and the start of shirts

explanation.surface: A rough cloth that is used to make stretchy shirts.
explanation.definitionFit: Crash is a coarse linen or cotton fabric used for towels and curtains.

clue.text: What'll make one change veal to duck? It's considerable

wordplay.words: What'll make one change veal to duck?
wordplay.note: the question asks for an instruction: swap one letter of veal for another and it becomes teal, a small duck

explanation.surface: A puzzling kitchen question about turning a calf into a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads as an instruction, V AS T: veal becomes teal.
explanation.definitionFit: Vast means huge or immense, a strong synonym for considerable.

clue.text: Cut back on fish, limiting recipe

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing within bounds, so the fish surrounds the letter

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Economise on fish by restricting the recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: R for recipe comes from the Rx on prescriptions, Latin recipe meaning 'take'.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrench is to economise or reduce spending.

clue.text: Bank charging nothing? Head should be forced to last!

indicators.text: Head should be forced to last!
indicators.note: the leading letter is pushed from the front to the very end

parts.note: a free service charges nothing

explanation.surface: A bank offering free service should force its boss to the back of the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: FREE with its first letter moved to the end gives REEF.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rock or sand near the surface of the sea, a sandbank.

clue.text: Aussie sledger (maybe) against pursuing moderation

parts.note: ho is an old word for a stop or limit, hence moderation
on can mean against, as in an attack on someone

explanation.surface: An Australian cricketer who taunts opponents is up against calls for restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: Sledging is cricket slang for verbally abusing the batsman, which is the sort of thing a hoon might do.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoon is Australian slang for a lout or hooligan, the sort who might sledge.

clue.text: Messenger more open to view clutching latest from battle

indicators.note: clutching means gripping tightly, so the first word wraps round a letter

parts.note: barer means more exposed or uncovered

indicators.note: the latest from a word is its final letter

parts.note: final letter of battle

explanation.surface: A courier, more exposed, carries the newest report from the battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: A bearer is one who carries a message or letter, so a messenger.

clue.text: Pen brief CV including last item in career

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the short résumé holds a letter

parts.note: bio is short for biography, a brief life summary

indicators.note: the last item in a word is its final letter

parts.note: final letter of career

explanation.surface: Write a short résumé, ending with your latest job.
explanation.definitionFit: Biro is the British trademark name for a ballpoint pen, used for any such pen.

clue.text: Not disputing a tennis set, injured

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so the letters are knocked out of shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A player accepts a lost tennis set without argument because of injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Assentient means agreeing or consenting, the opposite of disputing.

clue.text: Sandal wood (old-style) gate

indicators.note: wood is an archaic word for mad, and something mad is wildly disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wooden sandal and an old-fashioned wooden gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood' looks like timber, apt for a clog, but it is the old adjective meaning mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A geta is a Japanese wooden sandal raised on two crosspieces.

clue.text: Fairy's kept in by swirling snow, not wanting drill?

indicators.note: kept in by means held inside, so the fairy goes within the other letters
swirling means whirling about, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
an elf is a fairy, plus the S

explanation.surface: A fairy is trapped indoors by a blizzard and does not want to do exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drill' is the furrow seeds are sown in, not exercise; ELFS goes after the first S of SOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-sown plant grows from seed it dropped itself, needing no sowing in a drill.
